flippant

FLIP-uhnt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Flippant is not showing the seriousness or respect that a situation calls for -- treating a serious moment as if it were light or funny.

When a reporter asked about the delayed rescue effort, the official's flippant 'we're working on it' answer drew immediate criticism.

Example

Instead of taking the fire drill seriously, the new employee made a flippant joke about the alarm being 'a great excuse for a coffee break.'

Flippant describes a tone, not a fact -- it's about treating something serious as though it were unimportant or funny.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

breezy: Breezy describes a light, cheerful, relaxed manner -- a breezy chat, a breezy reply to a friend. On its own it disrespects nothing. A remark turns flippant only when that lightness lands on something serious: breezy is about ease, while flippant is about a mismatch.

irreverent: Irreverent describes a standing attitude or style that refuses to treat respected things -- traditions, authorities, solemn occasions -- as sacred. Flippant is smaller and situational: one remark treating one serious moment too lightly. A comedian's whole act can be irreverent; a single joke at the wrong time is flippant.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

solemn: deeply serious and formal

earnest: sincere and serious in intention

Where it sits · how little respect it shows

offhand → flippant → dismissive

offhand vs. flippant: An offhand comment is just casual and unplanned -- it doesn't necessarily disrespect the topic the way a flippant one does.

dismissive vs. flippant: Dismissive goes further than flippant, actively brushing a serious concern aside rather than just joking about it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — flip-: to move quickly, toss carelessly (probably imitative/Scottish dialect)

suffix — -ant: having the quality of (Latin -antem)

Put it together: Flippant likely grew out of flip -- to toss something quickly and carelessly. A flippant remark is tossed off the same way: quick, careless, and without the seriousness the moment actually deserves.

Use the root in a new word: flippancy: Flippancy is the noun form -- a flippant attitude or remark.

Word Choice

Flippant is about mismatched tone -- treating something serious lightly -- so it almost always shows up alongside a situation that clearly called for more respect.
